title: Electromagnetism / Electrodynamics
description: Electromagnetism / Electrodynamics develops the modern field-theoretic view of electric and magnetic phenomena. Students progress from electrostatics, magnetostatics, boundary-value methods, materials, and Maxwell's equations to waves, guided systems, radiation, relativistic formulation, computational modeling, and original technical work.

topics.title: Vector Calculus, Distributions, and Boundary-Value Methods for Fields
topics.description: Students build the mathematical language needed to treat fields locally, globally, and across boundaries.

children.title: Vector operators and coordinate systems
children.description: The point is to describe fields precisely in the geometries where physical problems actually live.

children.title: Integral theorems
children.description: Students learn how local field laws become global balance laws over volumes, surfaces, and loops.

children.title: Physical interpretation of flux and circulation
Distributions and singular sources
children.description: Point charges, ideal dipoles, and surface sources require disciplined use of delta functions.

topics.title: Electrostatics, Coulomb's Law, and Electric Potential
topics.description: This module develops static electric fields from charges, potentials, symmetry, and field equations.

children.title: Coulomb field and superposition
children.description: Students see electric fields as vector sums generated by discrete and continuous charge distributions.

children.title: Gauss's law
children.description: Gauss's law turns symmetry into a powerful shortcut and reveals the local source-field relationship.

children.title: Potential, Laplace equation, and Poisson equation
children.description: Potential methods convert vector field problems into scalar boundary-value problems.

topics.title: Boundary Conditions, Conductors, Dielectrics, and Energy in Electric Fields
topics.description: Students learn how electric fields behave at material interfaces and how field energy is stored and transferred.

children.title: Conductors and boundary conditions
children.description: Conductors impose strong constraints that make many electrostatic problems solvable.

children.title: Dielectrics and polarization
children.description: Materials alter electric fields through bound charge and polarization response.

children.title: Energy, capacitance, and field stress
children.description: Students connect field configurations to stored energy, forces, and measurable device behavior.

topics.title: Multipole Expansions, Green Functions, and Special Techniques
topics.description: This topic provides high-level methods for solving real electrostatic problems beyond simple symmetry.

children.title: Multipole expansion
children.description: Far-field structure is organized by total charge, dipole moment, quadrupole moment, and higher corrections.

children.title: Method of images and conformal ideas
children.description: Special geometries can be solved by replacing boundaries with equivalent source systems.

children.title: Green functions and separation of variables
children.description: These are the core graduate tools for solving electrostatics in nontrivial domains.

topics.title: Magnetostatics, Vector Potential, and Magnetic Materials
topics.description: Students study steady currents, magnetic fields, vector potentials, and matter's magnetic response.

children.title: Biot-Savart law and Ampere's law
children.description: Students derive magnetic fields from steady currents using direct integration and symmetry.

children.title: Vector potential
children.description: The vector potential makes magnetostatics structurally parallel to electrostatics and prepares students for gauge theory.

children.title: Magnetic matter
children.description: Real media respond magnetically through magnetization, bound currents, and material laws.

children.title: Linear, dia-, para-, and ferromagnetic response

topics.title: Electromagnetic Induction, Quasistatics, and Maxwell's Equations
topics.description: This module completes the transition from static fields to the unified time-dependent field theory.

children.title: Faraday induction
children.description: Time-varying magnetic flux produces electric fields and practical electromotive force.

children.title: Quasistatic approximations
children.description: Students learn when circuits and slowly varying fields can be treated without the full wave problem.

children.title: Maxwell's equations
children.description: Displacement current completes the field equations and predicts electromagnetic waves.

topics.title: Conservation Laws, Potentials, and Gauge Freedom
topics.description: Students learn how electrodynamics encodes energy, momentum, and equivalent potential descriptions.

children.title: Poynting theorem
children.description: Energy conservation in fields explains power flow, losses, and storage outside circuit idealizations.

children.title: Momentum and stress
children.description: Fields carry momentum and exert forces that can be computed through stress tensors.

children.title: Potentials and gauge transformations
children.description: Different potentials can describe the same fields, and gauge choice is a tool rather than a nuisance.

topics.title: Electromagnetic Waves in Vacuum and Media
topics.description: This topic develops wave propagation, polarization, dispersion, attenuation, and energy flow from Maxwell's equations.

children.title: Plane waves in vacuum
children.description: Students derive propagating fields directly from source-free Maxwell equations.

children.title: Polarization
children.description: Polarization captures the vector structure of waves and is central to optics, antennas, and scattering.

children.title: Waves in material media
children.description: Media change propagation through permittivity, permeability, loss, and dispersion.

topics.title: Reflection, Refraction, Waveguides, and Transmission Lines
topics.description: Students connect field theory to interfaces, guided propagation, RF systems, and engineering transmission models.

children.title: Interfaces and Fresnel physics
children.description: Boundary conditions at interfaces determine reflected and transmitted field amplitudes.

children.title: Brewster angle and total internal reflection
Transmission lines
children.description: Distributed voltage-current models emerge from field theory and support RF design.

children.title: Waveguides and cavities
children.description: Boundary conditions can confine waves into discrete modes with cutoff frequencies.

topics.title: Radiation from Charges, Antennas, and Scattering
topics.description: This module explains how accelerated charges emit radiation and how fields interact with objects and antennas.

children.title: Retarded potentials and moving charges
children.description: Causality requires fields to depend on source behavior at earlier times.

children.title: Dipole radiation and antennas
children.description: Simple radiators reveal how currents launch waves into space.

children.title: Scattering and radiation interaction
children.description: Students learn how fields exchange energy and momentum with particles and structures.

topics.title: Relativistic Electrodynamics and Covariant Field Theory
topics.description: Students see electricity and magnetism as one relativistic field theory expressed cleanly in spacetime language.

children.title: Special relativity foundations
children.description: Electromagnetism motivates and is clarified by Lorentz symmetry.

children.title: Field transformations
children.description: Electric and magnetic fields mix under changes of inertial frame.

children.title: Covariant Maxwell equations
children.description: The full theory becomes compact and elegant in tensor notation.

topics.title: Electrodynamics in Matter, Dispersion, Loss, and Plasmas
topics.description: This topic extends Maxwell theory to real media whose response depends on frequency, structure, and carrier dynamics.

children.title: Linear response and constitutive models
children.description: Matter is modeled through response functions that connect microscopic behavior to macroscopic fields.

children.title: Lossy and dispersive propagation
children.description: Students learn how absorption, conductivity, and dispersion reshape electromagnetic waves.

children.title: Plasmas, metamaterials, and engineered media
children.description: Modern electrodynamics includes media whose effective response can be designed or tuned.

topics.title: Numerical and Computational Electromagnetics
topics.description: Students learn how modern electrodynamics problems are modeled, simulated, verified, and interpreted computationally.

children.title: Finite-difference and FDTD methods
children.description: Grid-based methods turn Maxwell equations into time-stepped simulations.

children.title: Finite element and method of moments
children.description: Frequency-domain and integral-equation methods solve complex geometries and radiation problems.

children.title: Verification and interpretation
children.description: Simulation is only useful when its assumptions, convergence, and physical checks are explicit.

topics.title: Electrodynamics Project: Experiment, Simulation, or Theory
topics.description: The course culminates in a rigorous project that integrates modeling, calculation, validation, and scientific communication.

children.title: Project framing
children.description: Students convert a physical question into a tractable electrodynamics model or measurement plan.

children.title: Execution and validation
children.description: High-quality work compares theory, computation, and measurement wherever possible.

children.title: Communication
children.description: The final product should read like a concise technical paper or design report.
